# Step 4 — Open Configuration PR (setup lane)

Open the pull request for the branch created in step 3. This step only creates
the GitHub PR; no working-tree changes happen here.

## Open the PR

Do NOT commit to `<BASE_BRANCH>` directly. Open the PR from the branch pushed
in step 3:

```bash
gh pr create \
  --title "ci: configure Mergify auto-merge rules" \
  --body "Auto-merge every green, non-draft PR via Mergify merge queue. Auto-generated by pr-babysit setup.

Config customizations:
- Base branch: <BASE_BRANCH>
- CI checks: <comma-separated>
- Checks timeout: <duration>
- Max parallel checks: <N>
- Merge method: <method>
- Update method: <method>
- Required approvals: <N>
- Priority rules: <yes|no>
- Stale cleanup: <yes|no>
- Welcome comment: <yes|no>
- Keep PRs up to date: <yes|no>" \
  --base <BASE_BRANCH> \
  --head chore/configure-mergify-rules \
  --label setup
```

Report: "Created PR #<N> to configure Mergify merge rules. Once merged, green non-draft PRs will auto-merge via the Mergify merge queue."

## Report 

> Setup PR: #<N> (https://github.com/<REPO_NAME>/pull/<N>)
> Base branch: <BASE_BRANCH>
> Label: setup
> Config file: .github/mergify.yml

## Next

After the PR merges (via Mergify queue or direct merge once CI is green), continue
to **step 5** (register in Orca event automation) so the new repo's `pr_opened`,
`ci_failed`, and other events fire. The setup lane is complete after step 5.

If the repo also needs release setup, that is owned by Risa-AutoRelease
(`releasing` skill), not this skill.
